title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from cote 137 and the neighbouring pages). k is a ring, B a k-additive category, and \mathcal P_* is a category of half-simplicial (semi-simplicial: face maps only, no degeneracies) objects. It carries distinguished objects \Psi^i_*. Grothendieck works with a nested chain of subcategories \mathcal P_* \supset \mathcal Q_*=\mathcal P_{1*} \supset \mathcal P_{0*} \supset \mathcal K_*, and a parallel chain \mathcal P \supset \mathcal Q \supset \mathcal P_0 \supset \mathcal K.
- \mathcal K is the subcategory of 'negligible' objects, probably the \partial-perfect or acyclic ones.
- \mathcal P_0 and \mathcal P_1 are presumably generated by \Psi^0 and by \Psi^0,\Psi^1, modulo \mathcal K.

On the previous page he set up Σ-injective and Σ-projective resolutions in \mathcal P. He identified the category of (k-additive, Σ-) functors F:\mathcal P\to B with cochain complexes C^\cdot in B, via F\mapsto F(\Psi^0) \leftrightarrow Z^0(C^\cdot). He then defined H^i(F)=R^iF(\Psi^0), which is H^i(C^\cdot) for i\ge1, with RF(\Psi^0)\simeq F(C^\cdot). So \mathcal P is a kind of universal or 'generic' category: additive functors out of it are complexes. The objects \Psi^i play the role of the shifted unit k[-i].

This page:
1. It finishes that point: the identification holds in the derived category because the chosen object is a Σ-injective resolution of \Psi^0.
2. It introduces a multiplicative structure. The degreewise tensor product of half-simplicial objects is (L_*\otimes M_*)_{[n]} = L_{[n]}\otimes M_{[n]}. It comes with associativity, unit and commutativity constraints; the unit is \Psi^0_* = \mathbb 1_* (the constant object).
3. Ideal and stability properties:
   - \mathcal K_* is a \otimes-ideal: if one factor lies in \mathcal K_*, so does the product.
   - \mathcal P_0 is stable under \otimes because \Psi^0\otimes\Psi^0\simeq\Psi^0, i.e. \mathbb 1\otimes\mathbb 1=\mathbb 1.
   - \mathcal Q=\mathcal P_1 is stable under \otimes because \Psi^i\otimes\Psi^j\simeq\Psi^{i+j} \oplus (an object of \mathcal K).
   The last relation is an Eilenberg–Zilber / cup-product statement: modulo the negligible ideal, the \Psi^i form a graded monoid, like k[-i]\otimes k[-j]=k[-i-j].
4. The symmetric monoidal structure is transported, under the equivalences, to \mathcal P and its subcategories (written * to avoid confusion), and to the other realizations \mathcal P_\cdot, \mathcal P^*, \mathcal P^\cdot (covariant and contravariant variants). The next page checks that the equivalences \rho_*, \rho^* are compatible with \otimes. It then defines a 'multiplicative structure' on an additive functor F:B'\to B between symmetric monoidal additive categories: u_{X,Y}:F(X)\otimes F(Y)\to F(X\otimes Y) and \mathbb 1\to F(\mathbb 1), compatible with the associativity, unit and commutativity constraints. That is a lax symmetric monoidal functor.

Purpose. The aim is to obtain cup products on the cohomology H^i(F)=R^iF(\Psi^0) of a multiplicative F. Since \mathcal P is universal for complexes, this would give a canonical, universal source for multiplicative structures on derived functors and on cohomology of (half-)simplicial complexes. This fits the 'dévissage … et structures multiplicatives' title of the file.
errors: The relation \Psi^i\otimes\Psi^j\simeq\Psi^{i+j} + (element of \mathcal K) is asserted without proof. For half-simplicial objects (no degeneracies) the usual Eilenberg–Zilber shuffle map is not available. Only the Alexander–Whitney direction uses faces alone. So the claim needs a separate argument, or depends on the specific definition of \Psi^i and \mathcal K, which the page does not show.
The phrase 'si un des facteurs L_*, M_* est des K_*, l'autre aussi' must mean 'the product is in K_*' (ideal property), not 'the other factor is'. As written it is a slip of the pen.
The listed constraints read 'contraintes d'ass., comm. (\Psi^0), et de commut.'. The first 'comm.' is surely 'unité' (\Psi^0 = unit object), otherwise commutativity is listed twice.

ideas.what: Degreewise tensor product on (half-)simplicial objects as a symmetric monoidal structure with unit the constant object
ideas.modern_name: levelwise (pointwise) monoidal structure on simplicial objects

ideas.what: Negligible objects \mathcal K form a \otimes-ideal, so the tensor descends to the quotient
ideas.modern_name: thick tensor ideal / tensor structure on Verdier or additive quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; systematized by Balmer (2005) in tt-geometry

ideas.what: \Psi^i\otimes\Psi^j\simeq\Psi^{i+j} modulo \mathcal K: the generators of the universal category behave as shifted units, a graded monoid giving cup products
Transport of the monoidal structure to a universal additive category \mathcal P whose additive functors to B are complexes in B, with derived functors H^i(F)=R^iF(\Psi^0)
ideas.modern_name: universal property of complexes / Day-convolution-type monoidal structure on a generic category
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (cf. Day convolution 1970; Freyd universal abelian categories)

ideas.what: Multiplicative structure on an additive functor (next page): u_{X,Y}, unit map, coherence diagrams
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bénabou, Eilenberg–Kelly (1966); Saavedra Rivano (1972, Grothendieck's student)
ideas.where_published: related ⊗-functor formalism in Saavedra's thesis (Grothendieck school)

missed.claim: A programme to obtain cup products on derived functors universally: put a symmetric monoidal structure on the generic half-simplicial category \mathcal P (whose additive functors are complexes), show the \Psi^i form a graded monoid modulo the ideal \mathcal K, and transport this to all realizations. This is an early, half-simplicial and non-model-categorical version of monoidal Dold–Kan and of multiplicative derived functors. The half-simplicial Eilenberg–Zilber step is not carried out on this page.
missed.quote: \Psi^i_{*}\otimes\Psi^j_{*}\simeq\Psi^{i+j}_{*} + élément de K (\Rightarrow stabilité de \mathcal P_{1*}=\mathcal Q)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Monoidal structures on semi-simplicial objects are notoriously delicate (no degeneracies). A worked half-simplicial cup-product formalism via a universal category would interest people working on semi-simplicial models and monoidal Dold–Kan. It is likely superseded by Schwede–Shipley and by ∞-categorical methods (Lurie).

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up standard material: a levelwise tensor product, a tensor ideal, and the transport of a symmetric monoidal structure, leading into the definition of lax monoidal functors. The only mildly distinctive point is applying this to Grothendieck's half-simplicial universal category \mathcal P, with \Psi^i\otimes\Psi^j=\Psi^{i+j} mod \mathcal K. That is unverified here and conceptually close to known Eilenberg–Zilber / monoidal Dold–Kan results.
transcription_corrections: Second chain likely reads '\mathcal P\supset\mathcal Q\supset\mathcal P_0\supset\mathcal K' (parallel to \mathcal P_*\supset\mathcal Q_*\supset\mathcal P_{0*}\supset\mathcal K_*), not '\mathcal Q_0'.
'contraintes d'ass., comm. (\Psi^0), et de commut.' should probably read 'contraintes d'ass., d'unité (\Psi^0), et de commut.'
'K_* est une *-idéal' should read 'K_* est un \otimes-idéal' (ideal for the levelwise tensor).
'(ou deux des ...)' at the bottom likely reads 'ou deux des variantes contravariantes'; 'variantes' / 'réalisations' is uncertain.

Bottom line: '\otimes ou \overset{*}{\otimes} sur \mathcal P^*, ou les équivalences' likely continues 'où les équivalences [\rho_* avec \rho^*] sont compatibles avec \otimes' (continued on the next page).
